messages:
maria (eng-platform): FYI — saw a canary run where sampling + coalesce window caused an unredacted snippet to show up in telemetry. logs show request-phase scrubbed, but the coalesced item retained the original in the metric payload. :grimacing:

Derek (eng-ml): ugh. do we know if this is a routing edge (multiple backends) or a batching/coalesce bug in the telemetry emitter?

maria (eng-platform): looks like coalesce + fallback routing. timeline: req -> ingress scrub -> queued for batch -> routed to fallback model -> response triggers merge+emit. merge used original cached payload for metrics.

sam (eng-infra): thinking out loud: our current coalesce key is route+prompt-hash+tenant. if fallback replaces model but preserves original payload id, the coalesce layer may merge pre-scrub and post-scrub variants. we should treat "redaction-level" as part of the coalesce key.

olivia (eng-sre): big concern for oncall: any leak of PII to metrics/observability is high-sev. we need a fail-closed path: if redaction-level mismatch detected, drop the metric rather than emit.

anna (privacy): agree. also need audit trail: when metrics are dropped we must store an encrypted audit event (with KMS) accessible only to compliance. cannot silently drop for investigations.

Derek (eng-ml): metrics we might need: route.sampled.requests, route.redacted.count (labels: route, tenant, redaction_level), sampler.coalesce.dropped_reason. that lets us see drops without payloads.

maria (eng-platform): proposal: add 2 changes — (1) include redaction_level + redact_version in coalesce key, (2) emitter enforces emit_policy: -> if key mismatch or unknown redaction_level => emit metadata-only metric and increment sampler.coalesce.dropped_reason=policy_mismatch. no payload attached.

sam (eng-infra): implementation sketch:
```yaml
routes:
  - id: /v1/generate
    sampling:
      enabled: true
      redaction_level: strict   # none | minimal | strict
      coalesce_window_ms: 50
      coalesce_key_parts: [route, prompt_hash, redact_version]
```
coalesce code: add compare on redact_version before merging payloads. if mismatch -> drop payload, emit metadata-only metric instead.

olivia (eng-sre): how do we handle response-phase redaction? sometimes PII only appears in model output (not request). coalescing at request-time won't protect that.

maria (eng-platform): right — we need a two-phase scrub: request-phase scrub asap for ingress logs + routing, and response-phase scrub just before emit. coalesce may only carry metadata until response-phase completes. coalesce window can be extended slightly to wait for response-phase if route is flagged as high-risk.

anna (privacy): that two-phase flow is acceptable if we ensure encrypted audit logs and clear TTL for temporary unredacted buffers. define strict TTL (e.g., 60s) for any temp unredacted object and require HSM/KMS-wrapped keys; access controls for breakglass.

Derek (eng-ml): UX for console: add an observability card for "redaction hygiene" per-route: percent metrics emitted as metadata-only, recent drops, and canary annotations. sample query suggestion:
```
sum by(route,redaction_level) (rate(route.redacted.count[5m]))
sum by(route) (rate(sampler.coalesce.dropped_reason{reason="policy_mismatch"}[5m]))
```
This keeps numbers but never exposes raw text.

sam (eng-infra): performance impact: adding redact_version to coalesce key increases cardinality. we should default redact_version to a short stable id per release, and only bump when redaction logic changes. also provide a console toggle per-tenant to opt into more aggressive coalesce (less cardinality) vs strict safety.

olivia (eng-sre): rollouts: start with new canary flag "coalesce_strict_mode" off by default. enable on 1-2 low-traffic tenants, monitor sampler.coalesce.dropped_reason, route.redacted.count. if spikes look good, expand. plan for quick revert to fail-open to preserve availability, but require policy to flip to fail-closed when compliance tenants enabled.

anna (privacy): don't allow fail-open for regulated tenant orgs. those should always default to strict/fail-closed. add an org-level policy check at routing admission.

maria (eng-platform): open question: do we want an API-level flag so SDKs can opt into pre-hashing PII before sending (client-side pseudonymization)? pros: reduces server burden. cons: breaks server-side redaction auditing. thoughts?

Derek (eng-ml): would help some customers, but we still need server-side verification. can be an opt-in helper, not a replacement.

olivia (eng-sre): ops checklist for rollout:
- add telemetry counters (no payloads)
- add redact_version to coalesce key
- implement fail-closed path + metadata-only emit
- add canary flag + console card
- verify KMS/HSM audit flow
- run chaos test for routing fallback merging

sam (eng-infra): i'll open a PR for the coalesce change and a small feature branch for the emitter. aiming for a dev-canary next week.

maria (eng-platform): i'll draft a short console UX mock and the observability queries, tag QA + privacy.

anna (privacy): i'll write the compliance notes and required access policy for audit logs.

console-bot: canary rollouts: deployment scheduled for 4812410000, canary tenants: ten-omega, ten-beta. monitor channel: #eng-sre.

olivia (eng-sre): ack. please @me when PR ready. :eyes:

Derek (eng-ml): thanks, all. quick thumbs if you agree with the plan. :thumbsup:

sam (eng-infra): +1
anna (privacy): +1
olivia (eng-sre): +1
Derek (eng-ml): cool — closing out with action items in the thread.

maria (eng-platform): thanks — will sync next week after dev-canary results. :party:
